<description>
### Problem

When bitcoind starts and the HTTP IPv4 listen address is occupied by another process, but the IPv6 address is available, the server fails open and generates a cookie file. When bitcoin-cli runs it picks up the cookie file and sends the credentials in plain text to the non-bitcoind process running on the default IPv4 port. An attacker can then use the credentials to commandeer bitcoind over IPv6.

### Solution

*Safe defaults*:
* When running with default settings, require that the IPv4 bind succeeds.
* When `-rpcbind` is specified, require that all HTTP listen socket binds succeed (fail closed-behavior).

Node operators who only have IPv6 are now required to override `-rpcbind` and `-rpcallowip` to only specify the working interface and allowed subnet if they were not doing so already.

The problem of bitcoin-cli sending the credentials to what could possibly be the wrong process remains **only in non-default setups**.

### History

40b556d3742a1f65d67e2d4c760d0b13fe8be5b7 from 2015 switched the HTTP server from Boost Asio to LibEvent, and binding switched from an attempt at dual-binding IPv4+v6 and falling back to IPv4-only (rpcserver.cpp / `StartRPCThreads()`), to binding IPv4 *or* IPv6 (httpserver.cpp / `HTTPBindAddresses()`). **The current PR restores the prior behavior of IPv4 being mandatory.**

#14968 from 2018 was an attempt to change the behavior to require *all* binds to succeed. But it ran into issues with poor IPv6 support on CI.

### Severity

This credential exfiltration attack requires capability to launch processes on the bitcoind host. If we are on the same account we can already read the cookie credentials off disk. So it's only really interesting when an attacker is on a different user account on the same host.
</description>

[2026-11-18] rc:4615353481 inline on test/functional/rpc_bind.py by janb84 (member) (edited 2026-11-18):
Nit, non-block. Adding something like the test below will fix 2 of the gaps in test as reported by corecheck.

```suggestion

    def run_optional_ipv6_bind_test(self):
        self.log.info('Check that the node starts on IPv4 when the default IPv6 RPC address is already owned')
        self.nodes[0].rpchost = None
        with socket.create_server(('::1', self.defaultport), family=socket.AF_INET6):
            with self.nodes[0].assert_debug_log([f"Binding RPC on optional address '[::1]:{self.defaultport}' failed:"]):
                self.start_node(0, ['-disablewallet', '-nolisten'])
            assert_equal(set(get_bind_addrs(self.nodes[0].process.pid)), {(addr_to_hex('127.0.0.1'), self.defaultport)})
            self.stop_node(0)

    def run_unbindable_bind_test(self):
        self.log.info('Check that startup fails when an explicit RPC address cannot be bound, even if others succeed')
        # 192.0.2.1 (TEST-NET-1, RFC 5737) is not assigned to a local interface,
        # so bind() fails with EADDRNOTAVAIL rather than EADDRINUSE.
        extra_args = ['-disablewallet', '-nolisten', '-rpcallowip=127.0.0.1', '-rpcbind=127.0.0.1', '-rpcbind=192.0.2.1']
        with self.nodes[0].assert_debug_log([
            f"Binding RPC on address '127.0.0.1:{self.defaultport}'",
            f"Binding RPC on required address '192.0.2.1:{self.defaultport}' failed:",
        ]):
            self.nodes[0].assert_start_raises_init_error(extra_args, 'Error: Unable to start HTTP server. See debug log for details.')

    def run_unresolvable_bind_test(self):
        self.log.info('Check that startup fails when an explicit RPC address is not numeric, even if others are')
        extra_args = ['-disablewallet', '-nolisten', '-rpcallowip=127.0.0.1', '-rpcbind=127.0.0.1', '-rpcbind=localhost']
        with self.nodes[0].assert_debug_log(
            [f"Could not lookup RPC bind address 'localhost' port {self.defaultport} (only numeric addresses are allowed)."],
            unexpected_msgs=["Binding RPC on address"],  # fails before any bind is attempted
        ):
            self.nodes[0].assert_start_raises_init_error(extra_args, 'Error: Unable to start HTTP server. See debug log for details.')

```

[2026-11-18] c:6991339559 comment by hodlinator (member):
Thanks for the review @janb84! As stated out-of-band, starting to write the release notes you suggested motivated me to look into being less harsh on IPv6-only hosts.

Upon failure to bind the IPv4 loopback port, we could create an IPv4 socket and try to bind it to a random ephemeral port. If that *also* fails, we could assume that we don't have an IPv4 stack at all and let the IPv6-only bind be sufficient. I'll need some more time to investigate this.
